The core insight of ADR-0005 is that traditional sports analytics treat game picks, player props, and DFS lineups as independent domains, leading to internal inconsistencies and missed arbitrage opportunities. The solution adopts a unified engine that generates stochastic game trajectories, which are then used to derive coherent decisions across all three domains. This approach leverages the mathematical structure of probability distributions and optimization theory to ensure consistency. The cross-derivative contradiction detector uses KL divergence to identify when bookmaker pricing is inconsistent across related markets. The unified engine uses Pyomo MILP for DFS lineup construction and pyribs MAP-Elites for exploring diverse situational outcomes. This creates a closed-loop system where each domain feeds back into the others through shared probabilistic models. The failure mode occurs when model assumptions break down—such as when external factors like weather or injuries are not captured in the simulation. The system's robustness depends on maintaining the integrity of the underlying stochastic process and ensuring that all derived decisions remain within the bounds of the original probability space.
